text: Photography relies on two primary components: the shutter and the aperture. The shutter dictates light duration by determining how long the sensor receives illumination, whereas the aperture regulates the width of the lens opening for light entry. To capture images under low-light conditions, one must select a wider aperture alongside a slower shutter speed. Conversely, freezing fast motion, such as that of a moving vehicle, requires a quicker shutter speed paired with a larger aperture. Ultimately, these two elements combine to facilitate successful image capture.
